acv.quote: Two hundred and fifty K ACV.

header.reason: Halima, the COO who made the call, wanted a named person and an escalation path for on-sale mornings. The competitor brought its real account team and promised on-call cover, while we showed tiered support plans. Jordan believes we were the better platform and that the load test had won it, but Halima's only reaction to the load test was 'good'.

findings.label: What started it
findings.finding: Aim messaging at the moment payments fail minutes into a big on-sale and nobody answers, when executives are watching publicly.
findings.quote: payments started failing about four minutes in. Their provider's support was a ticket form. They got a reply after the on-sale was over.

findings.label: Who decided
findings.finding: Arm reps to pitch the COO directly on who responds during an on-sale, rather than relying on the CTO to carry the technical results.
findings.quote: it was Halima's call and she made it in one meeting.

findings.label: The competitor
findings.finding: Pre-empt the competitor by bringing our named solutions engineer and account lead to the decider meeting; the over-promising claim is only Jordan's untested guess.
findings.quote: A named solutions engineer and an account lead, in the room.

findings.label: Our message
findings.finding: Stop answering 'who's my person' with support tiers and response times; answer with a named contact and an escalation path for on-sale days.
findings.quote: so it's a queue with a faster timer.

findings.label: Missing proof
findings.finding: Build a written on-sale morning plan with solutions engineering, and recruit a ticketing reference who can say who picked up during a big on-sale.
findings.quote: She wanted to see, on paper, what we do on an on-sale morning. Who's watching, who she calls, what happens at minute four.

findings.label: Their words
findings.finding: Use 'what happens when it's down', 'a name, not a queue' and 'on-sale morning' instead of uptime and support-plan language.
findings.quote: I don't buy uptime, I buy what happens when it's down.
